items.title: Ken Poston interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 4, 2024
items.q: And so I had come across Chet Baker. And Chet was actually one that I could actually somewhat play along with.

ctx.x: I’m sorry, was Gerry Mulligan in your consciousness at that time?

Maybe through Chet Baker. Because when I really started to get interested in jazz I would have probably been eighth or ninth grade, and I was trying to find records of trumpet players even though I didn’t — maybe didn’t know who they were — to play along with, or to try to play with. And so I had come across Chet Baker. And Chet was actually one that I could actually somewhat play along with. Miles, you know, a little bit, but then Dizzy Gillespie, you know no. You know I found a Dizzy Gillespie record and you…
How about Maynard Ferguson, right? Oh there’s an easy one.
